Denote Sn the set of permutations in [n] and µ = µn the uniform distribution on Sn. In addition, denote by ν = νn the uniform distribution on {−1,+1}n. We will use the following notation conventions for graphs.

- • Labeled graphs. Denote by Kn the complete graph with vertex set [n] and edge set Un. For any graph H, let V (H) denote the vertex set of H and let E(H) denote the edge set of H. We say H is a subgraph of G, denoted by H ⊂ G, if V (H) ⊂ V (G) and E(H) ⊂ E(G). We say φ : V (H) → V (S) is an injection, if for all (i,j) ∈ E(H) we have (φ(i),φ(j)) ∈ E(S).

For H,S ⊂ Kn, denote by H ∩ S the graph with vertex set given by V (H) ∩ V (S) and edge set given by E(H) ∩ E(S), and denote by S ∪ H the graph with vertex set given by V (H) ∪ V (S) and edge set given by E(H) ∪ E(S). For any graph H, denote the excess of H by τ(H) = |E(H)| − |V (H)|. Given u ∈ V (H), define NeiH(u) to be the set of neighbors of u in H. For two vertices u,v ∈ V (H), we define DistH(u,v) to be their graph distance. Denote the diameter of a connected graph H by Diam(H) = maxu,v∈V (H) DistH(u,v).

- • Graph isomorphisms and unlabeled graphs. Two graphs H and H′ are isomorphic, denoted by H ∼= H′, if there exists a bijection π : V (H) → V (H′) such that (π(u),π(v)) ∈ E(H′) if and only if (u,v) ∈ E(H). Denote by H the isomorphism class of graphs; it is customary to refer to these isomorphic classes as unlabeled graphs. Let Aut(H) be the number of automorphisms of H (graph isomorphisms to itself). For any graph H, define Fix(H) = {u ∈ V (H) : φ(u) = u,∀φ ∈ Aut(H)}.
- • Induced subgraphs. For a graph H = (V,E) and a subset A ⊂ V , define HA = (A,EA) to be the induced subgraph of H in A, where EA = {(u,v) ∈ E : u,v ∈ A}. Also, define H\A = (V,E\A) to be the subgraph of H obtained by deleting all edges with both endpoints in A. Note that EA ∪ E\A = E.
- • Isolated vertices. For u ∈ V (H), we say u is an isolated vertex of H if there is no edge in E(H) incident to u. Denote I(H) as the set of isolated vertices of H.
- • Paths, self-avoiding paths and non-backtracking paths. We say a subgraph H ⊂ Kn is a path with endpoints u,v (possibly with u = v), if there exist w1,...,wm ∈ [n] ̸= u,v such that V (H) = {u,v,w1,...,wm} and E(H) = {(u,w1),(w1,w2)...,(wm,v)} (we allow the occurrence of multiple vertices or edges). We say H is a self-avoiding path if w0,w1,...,wm,wm+1 are distinct (where we denote w0 = u and wm+1 = v), and we say H is a non-backtracking path if wi+1 ̸= wi−1 for 1 ≤ i ≤ m. Denote EndP(P) as the set of endpoints of a path P.
- • Cycles and independent cycles. We say a subgraph H is an m-cycle if V (H) = {v1,...,vm} and E(H) = {(v1,v2),...,(vm−1,vm),(vm,v1)}. For a subgraph K ⊂ H, we say K is an independent m-cycle of H, if K is an m-cycle and no edge in E(H) \ E(K) is incident to V (K). Denote Cm(H) as the set of independent m-cycles of H. For H ⊂ S, we define Cm(S,H) to be the set of independent m-cycles in S whose vertex set is disjoint from V (H).
- • Leaves. A vertex u ∈ V (H) is called a leaf of H, if the degree of u in H is 1; denote L(H) as the set of leaves of H.
- • Trees and rooted trees. We say a graph T = (V (T),E(T)) is a tree, if T is connected and has no cycles. We say a pair (T,R(T)) is a rooted tree with root R(T), if T is a tree and R(T) ∈ V (T). For a rooted tree T and u ∈ V (T), we define DepT(u) = DistT(R(T),u) to be
